[descent_text] Key descent hazards mirror the approach: the exposed ridge-crest sections near the summit (do not descend this route if the ridge is snow-covered or wet — the exposed traverse becomes significantly more dangerous), loose rock on the steep lower ridge (rockfall risk onto anyone below — descend it one at a time), and the steep, rooted, ankle-turning tread on the 'mile from hell' switchbacks.

[turnaround] Turn back if snow or ice is present on the ridge, if any party member is not comfortable with the class 3 downclimb crux or the sustained exposure, or if thunderstorms are building given the fully exposed ridge walk with no bail-out shelter.

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.whyDry: Gullies typically melted out in peak season; snow is early July.
routes.quote: Peak dry-season conditions - gullies typically melted out, most consistent Class 3 rock scrambling
snowSentences: [overview] Cadet Peak (7,186 ft) rises above the Monte Cristo basin near Glacier Basin Falls and is the second-highest summit in the Monte Cristo Group after Kyes Peak.
[overview] The standard route is an exposed Class 3 scramble up the southwest-facing gullies and ridge above Glacier Basin, on slopes that hold snow well into summer;
[beta] From upper Glacier Basin, cross the creek and pick up a narrow gully (colored reddish by old mine tailings in summer) on Cadet's southwest flank.
[beta] In early season the route holds snow and a snow/ice axe-and-crampons kit is standard;
[hazards] steep snow gullies early .
[hazards] washed-out bridge / creek crossings near Monte Cristo townsite and on the Glacier Basin trail .
[obj_haz] Early-season snow and glissade-prone gully .
[obj_haz] High/fast creek crossings on approach during snowmelt .

routes.name: Southeast Slopes
routes.whyDry: Steep snow is May-June; by August a talus scramble.
routes.quote: By August it dries into loose Class 3 talus
snowSentences: [overview] the standard route reaches the middle summit, traditionally treated as the highpoint, via a gully and ridge on the mountain's west side — though a June 2023 theodolite survey found the south summit is roughly 7 inches taller and is technically the true highpoint, reached from the middle summit by a short, exposed low-5th-class step that this route includes as an optional finish.

[beta] From a basin camp roughly 6,800–7,100 ft below the peak, parties cross moderate snow/scree slopes toward the saddle between the north and middle summits, then follow the summit ridge (Class 2-3, with a couple of steep snow patches early season) to the non-technical middle summit (~8,590 ft).
[beta] When the north side holds snow, parties commonly drop onto the east/southeast slopes below the summit ridge (this route) rather than fight the icier north ridge.
[hazards] steep snow (40–50°) in the gully through June .
[obj_haz] steep snow to ~40° .
[gear] ice axe (essential through June on the summit gully) .
[gear] crampons (recommended May–June for 40–50° snow) .
[gear] sturdy boots suited to firm snow if climbing before mid-July .

routes.name: Flight of the Falcon
routes.whyDry: Basin snow only into early summer.
routes.quote: Summer, once the ford drops and the basin snow has gone .
snowSentences: [seasonal_guidance] Lingering snowpack buries some of the basin brush, but Squire Creek runs high with melt and the basin can still be snow-filled.
[best_season] the basin's approach terrain holds snow into early summer at this elevation and the brush is markedly worse when wet, so a stretch of settled, dry weather is recommended.
[approach_variants] Summer, once the ford drops and the basin snow has gone .
[approach_variants] Residual avalanche snow at the base early in the season .

routes.name: South Slopes
routes.whyDry: Saddle snow is early season; mid-July onward is snow-free scree.
routes.quote: Mid-July through September for dry, snow-free scree travel;
snowSentences: [beta] Parties continuing to North Gardner Mountain descend west along the summit ridge to a false summit, then drop and scramble through loose rock/scree (and snow in early season) to a saddle near Point 8487, from which the ridge continues north over Point 8487 to North Gardner.
[hazards] loose, exposed Class 2-3 rock and lingering steep snow on the crest between Point 8,487 and North Gardner .
[obj_haz] Avalanche hazard on Gardner's southern slopes when snow is present .
[watch_out] early-season snow in the saddle .
[gear] ice axe (early season) .
[gear] crampons (early-season snow on the ridge and north-facing gullies) .
[approach] This stretch is the route-finding crux of the approach: loose rock underfoot, and into early summer, lingering snow patches that can warrant an ice axe.

[descent_text] From Gardner's summit the route continues west along the summit ridge over a false summit, then descends steeply through loose scree and (early-season) snow to a saddle below Point 8487.

routes.name: West Face (5.9+ rock route)
routes.whyDry: Approach snow-free by the late-August window.
routes.quote: once the lakeside approach is snow-free
snowSentences: [beta] the approach is a short walk from the Smithbrook trailhead of about an hour, and it is an easier walk in than Snow Creek Wall.
[seasonal_guidance] Late August through September, once the lakeside approach is snow-free, the face is dry and the mosquitoes have died back .
[seasonal_guidance] Snow still covers the Union Gap trail and the benches below the wall, and the face stays wet from melt above.
[seasonal_guidance] The face is dry and the approach snow-free;
[seasonal_guidance] Short days and the first snow on the ledges quickly make loose, anchor-free rock serious;

[pro_tips] The approach is genuinely short for a Cascades wall — the 2002 party pitched it as an easier walk in than Snow Creek Wall — which makes it a reasonable objective for a late start or a marginal weather window.
[best_season] Summer and early autumn, roughly July through September, once the face is dry and the approach is snow-free.
[best_season] assume it is unclimbable once winter snow arrives.

routes.name: South Face
routes.whyDry: Col snow-free in the season.
routes.quote: Dry granite and a snow-free col;
snowSentences: [seasonal_guidance] Late July to mid-September, once the Crystal Creek gully is melted out and before autumn snow and short days .
[seasonal_guidance] Snow still fills the upper Crystal Creek basin and talus gully to the col, and Ingalls Creek runs high with melt;
[seasonal_guidance] Dry granite and a snow-free col;
[seasonal_guidance] Short days make the 10-plus mile approach and descent back to Ingalls Creek very long, and early snow on the slab crux removes the only safe way up.

[approach_variants] Little Annapurna is reached from the Upper Enchantments by an essentially class 1 walk-up and is often called the easiest Bulger — so if the terrain above you never becomes technical, you have wandered onto the ordinary walking side of the mountain rather than the south face, and the day is a hike, not a climb.

routes.name: Standard Trail (Upper Trailhead, NFR 24)
routes.whyDry: Summer trail is snow-free July-October; chute snow is spring.
routes.quote: In summer conditions (roughly July–October) the trail is snow-free
snowSentences: [overview] The mountain is best known regionally for its long, sun-exposed spring snow chute, one of the most reliable early-season glissades in the Olympics, and for the crowds it draws on summer weekends given its short approach relative to the payoff.
[hazards] Southeast-facing snow chute is an avalanche funnel that becomes sun-soaked and prone to wet slides by early-mid afternoon — start early and check NWAC in spring .
[hazards] Loss of the trail under snow leads to route-finding onto steeper, looser ground .
[obj_haz] Seasonal snow/avalanche chute (winter line) with fall/avalanche risk into early summer .
[gear] ice axe (early season) .

[approach] Here is a well-signed junction where the winter/climbers' route breaks right up the prominent scree-and-snow chute, while the maintained summer trail switchbacks left across rock-strewn slopes and gravelly subalpine meadows, many switchbacks having stairstep risers that add to the grade.

[approach] In summer conditions (roughly July–October) the trail is snow-free and well-cut essentially to the top, threading a narrow notch and crossing west-facing slopes before the final approach to the 5,944 ft summit — total gain from the Upper TH is 2,444 ft over 1.6 mi one-way.

[approach] Outside of core summer (roughly November–June), snow typically fills the chute and buries the upper switchbacks, and most parties climb the chute directly instead of the buried summer trail — this demands an ice axe and traction devices (crampons/microspikes), and the terrain is a steep, funnel-shaped slide path with real avalanche potential;

routes.name: Southeast Route
routes.whyDry: Snow chute is only the early-season option.
routes.quote: the snow chute is the early-season option and needs an axe.
snowSentences: [approach] the snow chute is the early-season option and needs an axe.
[descent_text] From the gap descend to the valley floor by the boulder gully, by the waterfall route beside it, or by the snow chute when it is soft;
[descent_text] hard early-season snow calls for an axe and crampons.

routes.name: Cloudy Peak Traverse (South Ridge)
routes.whyDry: No snow crossing described.
routes.quote: Mid-July through September, same window as the standard route;
snowSentences: [beta] A ridge-crest link between Cloudy Peak and North Star: from Cloudy Pass, scramble the ridge up to Cloudy Peak with expanding views toward Glacier Peak, Eldorado, and Buckner, on rock that is reasonably solid Class 4 with an option to keep it at Class 3.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.whyDry: Only early-season snow; route has no permanent snowfields or glaciers.
routes.quote: no permanent snowfields or glaciers on route
snowSentences: [overview] A small glacier clings to the peak's northeast slopes.
[beta] Descent is either back down the ridge or, early season, a steep glissade down snow on the north face.
[hazards] Steep snow on the north-face descent option requires an axe (and crampons if firm) - a fall here would be a long slide .
[hazards] Loose rock/scree on the north face once snow cover melts out .
[obj_haz] steep snow/glissade hazard on the north-face descent .
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons — early season, lingering snow on the ridge and the optional north-face glissade descent .
[descent] in early-mid season, some parties instead glissade/plunge-step the steep snow slopes on the north face.

[descent_text] In early season (roughly late May into mid-July), many parties instead glissade a long, steep snowfield on the north slope and traverse back to rejoin the West Ridge trail near 4,600 ft.

routes.name: Standard Route
routes.whyDry: Only residual early-July snow patches.
routes.quote: early July can still carry residual snow patches on the approach
snowSentences: [approach] Ford Ingalls Creek (a rock-hop in low water, but a genuine wet crossing during early-season snowmelt) and pick up the Ingalls Creek Trail, following it east/downstream about half a mile to the Beverly-Turnpike Trail junction at roughly 4,700 ft - the last dependable water source before the alpine basin above.
[seasonal_guidance] early July can still carry residual snow patches on the approach and cooler, damp rock .
[seasonal_guidance] Approach and surrounding terrain often still hold lingering snow;
[seasonal_guidance] rock can be wet or snow-covered, undermining the friction moves the route depends on .
[pro_tips] Start early to beat afternoon thunderstorms and catch any remaining approach snow while it's still firm .
[seasonal_hazards] N/A - non-glaciated summer rock route (Stuart Range / Alpine Lakes Wilderness climbed outside snow season) .
[seasonal_hazards] N/A - no glacier travel required to reach or climb the Balanced Rock itself (this is distinct from Sherpa Glacier-based routes on the main peak) .

[approach_variants] Ford the creek — a rock-hop in low water, a real wet crossing in snowmelt — and follow the Ingalls Creek Trail east about half a mile to the Beverly-Turnpike junction at about 4,700 ft.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.whyDry: North gully snow only into early July.
routes.quote: the north-facing approach gully holds snow into early July
snowSentences: [beta] The route passes around the balanced rock from the north side, which can involve a sketchy traverse over snow or wet rock in early season.
[obj_haz] snow/ice on the Balanced Rock traverse early season .
[seasonal_guidance] Warming and drying, though early-month snow/wet rock on north-facing steps can slow the exposed steps .
[seasonal_hazards] N/A - no glacier travel on this ridge route .
[best_season] the north-facing approach gully can hold snow into early July.
[approach_variants] the north-facing approach gully holds snow into early July .
[approach_variants] Snow lingering in the north-facing gully into early July .

routes.name: West Peak via West Ridge - West Face
routes.whyDry: August-September approach and ridge are snow-free.
routes.quote: Snow-free approach, low ford and dry ridge rock
snowSentences: [seasonal_guidance] August to September, when the long Park Lakes approach is snow-free and the Kachess ford is low, before fall snow .
[seasonal_guidance] early July can still hold snow patches on the west ridge.
[seasonal_guidance] Snow still covers the high Park Lakes basin and Spectacle Point camp, and the Kachess River ford runs high with melt.
[seasonal_guidance] Snow-free approach, low ford and dry ridge rock make the multi-day trip most straightforward;
[seasonal_guidance] The route has been climbed in mid-October, but an early storm can snow in the ridge, freeze camp water and shorten the days sharply.
[seasonal_guidance] Snow typically covers the west face and Spectacle Point, and the long remote approach leaves little margin in short days.

routes.name: Tower Arete
routes.whyDry: Season is once the cirque is melted out; snow is early season.
routes.quote: once the Tiffany Springs roads are clear and the cirque below the North Face is melted out
snowSentences: [approach] The North Face itself rises roughly 650 feet above the cirque, split by couloirs and a rock tower;
[seasonal_guidance] The gravel roads to Tiffany Springs are usually clear by mid-June, but snow can still fill the cirque and the lower arete.
[seasonal_guidance] Dry and snow-free, but water is scarce near the route and late-summer wildfire smoke often fills the Okanogan high country.
[seasonal_guidance] Snow can dust the North Face and the long gravel roads to 6,760 ft may be snowed over, making the drive the crux.
[seasonal_guidance] Cooler, calmer weather suits the loose arete, though early snow and cold mornings can arrive late in the month.
[pro_tips] The FA party completed this route on 6/16/15, so early-mid June timing may require additional snow considerations .
[best_season] June through early September, when snow has cleared from lower sections;
[approach_variants] The face rises around six hundred and fifty feet above the cirque and is split by couloirs and a rock tower.
